text: The Progress Rail PR43C was a 4,300 hp (3,210 kW) C-C genset diesel-electric locomotive developed by Progress Rail Services Corporation through the conversion of existing EMD SD50 locomotives. This conversion involved replacing the original EMD 645 prime mover with a 3,600 hp (2,680 kW) 12-cylinder Caterpillar C175 engine and a 700 hp (522 kW) Caterpillar C18 engine. The design was jointly created by Progress Rail and Norfolk Southern Railway, with development beginning in 2008. A total of three PR43Cs were built at Progress Rail's Mayfield, Kentucky factory. Two were used in revenue freight service on Norfolk Southern, while the third served as a demonstrator unit. Norfolk Southern had four additional PR43Cs on order at one time. These locomotives operated on freight trains in central Illinois, leading to speculation about testing due to Caterpillar's headquarters being located in Peoria, Illinois. The conversion altered the locomotive's external appearance, replacing the original radiator section with a larger one resembling that of an EMD SD70ACe or SD70M-2. Due to repeated mechanical failures, all PR43Cs were retired in 2017 and subsequently cut up for scrap in 2018. Prior to retirement, they were renumbered to prevent number conflicts with the AC44C6Ms.
